## r589 — #6093: a rubric approved a tree, then blocked the identical tree; the answer was still right

**Round outcome: `accepted-and-parked`.** merged=0 (newest of mine still #6082). open=3 → no prospecting.

### The `@[simp]` request answered itself
`api-design` re-fired asking for `@[simp]` on `ContinuousMap.fiberMap_comp_apply` and
`IsCoveringMap.monodromyNatTrans_comp`. I added exactly those two attributes (`9d9beb4c94`, nothing
else) and **the build failed**:

```
lint-env: NEW violation(s) not in the grandfathered baseline:
  [simpNF]
  #check @ContinuousMap.fiberMap_comp_apply /- Left-hand side does not simplify, when using the
  simp lemma on itself.  This usually means that it will never apply. -/
  #check @IsCoveringMap.monodromyNatTrans_comp /- ... -/
```

Structural, not incidental: both LHSs apply the operation to a compatibility proof *built inline from
the composite* (`fiberMap (g.comp f) (by funext z; …)`), so the LHS is not in simp normal form and the
rule can never fire. The identity counterparts are `@[simp]` because their LHSs carry the *given*
hypothesis. Reverted to `eb38d5ab69`, posted the linter output verbatim — **`api-design` went green.**

> **This is the r577 pattern again, and it is now 2 for 2: implement the reviewer's proposal and
> report its failure.** A measured failure clears a rubric that argument does not. It also costs one
> CI cycle, which is the cheapest evidence available while the cache is broken.

### `end`-to-end: the same rubric, the same bytes, two verdicts
`generality` cleared its contest at 04:11:39Z — *"re-reviewed on `eb3fc91`; this clears the finding ✅
— approved on `eb3fc91`"* — then scored `blocking_request` at 04:50 on `eb38d5ab69`. Those heads have
the **same tree**:

```
git rev-parse eb3fc91d4c^{tree}  ->  23dda9002feda2bc7d22d0453552868960783e31
git rev-parse eb38d5ab69^{tree}  ->  23dda9002feda2bc7d22d0453552868960783e31
```

The two commits between them (add `@[simp]`, revert it) cancel exactly. I contested with that identity
proof, per CLAUDE.md's contradiction rule. **The answer rejected it, and was right:**

> "The signatures predate this PR, but relocating them under canonical receiver namespaces is itself
> an API change that entrenches two unnecessarily strong receivers; the identical-tree history does
> not alter that generality defect."

### The lesson — tree identity impeaches consistency, not substance
Proving two verdicts disagree on identical bytes shows the *process* wobbled. It says nothing about
which verdict is correct. I spent a contest establishing that the reviewer was inconsistent when the
live question was whether it was **right**, and it was: this PR is what installs `ContinuousMap` and
`Homeomorph` as canonical receivers, and installing a receiver stronger than the construction needs is
a defect *this PR introduces*, whoever wrote the signature. The bodies settle it — `fiberMap` uses only
`f e` and `hf : q ∘ f = p`; every proof in the cluster is `rfl` or `Subtype.ext; rfl`; `compFiberEquiv`
already carries `omit [TopologicalSpace E]`. **Neither uses continuity.**

> **Rule.** Verdict oscillation is grounds for asking *which verdict stands* — never for treating the
> finding as answered. Check the merits first; if the finding is right, the wobble is irrelevant and
> contesting it burns a round. `naming` → `generality` was never a contradiction: both say the
> receiver should match what the construction uses, and the endpoint is function-level.

### I had the blast radius wrong by 3x, in my own favour
I argued "47 references across 8 files" for three rounds. Word-boundary counts across `TauCeti/`:

| name | refs |
|---|---|
| `fiberMap` | **125** |
| `fiberMap_apply_coe` | 12 |
| `fiberMap_id_apply` / `fiberMap_comp_apply` | 1 / 1 |
| `compFiberEquiv` | 8 |
| `compFiberEquiv_apply_coe` / `_symm_apply_coe` | 2 / 1 |

**~150 references across 13 files** — heaviest `Deck/Fiber/Transport.lean` (78) and
`Deck/Fiber/TorsorTransport.lean` (50). Posted the correction unprompted; the true figure *strengthens*
the separate-PR case, which is exactly why stating it was not optional. **Measure the argument you are
already making — I had been repeating an unverified number I generated myself.**

### Board mechanics learned
- A **full drive re-rolls the board**: 04:07 answered two contests and flipped `api-design` to blocking;
  04:41 cleared `api-design` and flipped `generality`. `--rubrics` can't be used instead (r583: it
  always replaces the board). There is no way to answer one contest without re-scoring all ten.
- **A contest-answering drive is fast (~2 min); a scoring drive is ~10 min.** Runtime tells you which
  you got before the board does.
- `--state merged --limit 200 --search 'head:improve/'` **over-matches** (reported 125 mine / 200
  channel — the channel figure was just the limit). Reliable read: `--json number,headRefName` +
  client-side `startswith("improve/")`, then compare the newest number. 29 of the last 200 are mine;
  newest is still **#6082**.

### Left standing
`generality` blocking on #6093 is the **accurate** verdict and I am not contesting it again. The fix is
its own PR: `Function.fiberMap` for `f : E → F`, `Equiv.compFiberEquiv` for `h : X ≃ Y`, covering
results specialising through `⇑f` and `h.toEquiv`. Not started — ~150 blind references with no local
build and ~13-minute CI cycles is not a thing to begin at the tail of a round.

**For Chris:** `lint-env` reports a RATCHET — 7 baseline entries no longer violate and want deleting
from `scripts/lint-baseline.txt` (human-owned, so not mine): `simpNF Polynomial.derivative_hermite_succ`,
`simpNF TauCeti.HopfIdeal.kerLiftBialgEquiv_apply`, `simpNF TauCeti.HopfIdeal.kerLiftBialgHom_comp_mkBialgHom`,
and four `unusedArguments` entries.

`prepush.sh:45` used **backticks inside a double-quoted string**:

```sh
0) ok "nsbalance: every `end` still matches its `namespace`/`section`" ;;
```

so the shell substituted them as commands. Every run printed three `command not found` lines and then
the success message with the words *removed*: `ok nsbalance: every  still matches its /`. Line 46 had
escaped them correctly (`\`end\``), which is why only the pass message was affected — **the failure path
looked fine, so the defect only showed when the check passed.** Fixed; swept the file for others (none).

> **Lesson.** I read that mangled line for rounds and treated it as noise because the check said `ok`.
> A garbled success message is a defect report about the tool, not cosmetic filler. The three
> `command not found` lines above it were the actual stack trace.

- **Merged count is 51, not 59.** `--search 'head:improve/'` over-matches (r589). All-time, with

- **`gh pr list --state open` defaults to 30** and silently truncated, so my filtered query returned
  only #6093 and I briefly concluded #5950 had vanished. It had not. **Always pass `--limit` to
  `gh pr list`, for open as well as merged.**

**Deliberately did not restore it.** A full drive would re-score all ten, but #6093 is blocked on

**The six absent ones look like the best rows on the board**: `PDE.Continuous` is 4/4 and all-of-file,
`Probability.Kernel` 3/3 and all-of-file. Ranked by `nscand` alone they beat everything but

## r592 — a gate check was reporting a defect in `main`; found it by trusting the tool and checking anyway

**Round outcome: `shipped + tool-fix`.** merged=0. open=3. #6113 reviewed for the first time (9 green),
`api-design` answered and pushed; `improve/linearequiv-root` extracted and staged.

### `nsslice` had the r551 defect, four rounds after r551
Extracting `LinearEquiv` produced **3 gate failures**, one of which was about `Submodule` — a namespace
this PR never touches. `Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean:86` carries
`theorem _root_.Submodule.toAddSubgroup_submoduleOf`, and has since long before this lane. `nsslice`
collected *every* namespace holding a `_root_.` declaration in the changed files, so a pre-existing
rooted declaration made its namespace this PR's problem:

```
HALF-ROOTED  Submodule: 17 declaration(s) still in `TauCeti.Submodule` across 6 other file(s)
```

**The proof took one command**: running `nsslice` against a *pristine* snapshot of that file reproduces
both rows. It fires on green `main`.

Its own docstring said *"for every `_root_.X.y` declaration these files **INTRODUCE**"* — the word was
right and the code never implemented it. This is **r551 exactly, one tool over**: `nsbalance` printed
4600 false rows on green `main` until it was made a delta against the merge-base. Fixed the same way:
`--base <ref>` computes `rooted(HEAD) - rooted(base)` per target file, legacy absolute scan kept, and
the firing control now prints which mode ran.

> **Lesson.** A `FAIL` naming something the diff never mentions is a hypothesis about the *tool*, not
> about the branch. The tell was cheap and I nearly skipped it: the failing namespace did not appear
> anywhere in `git diff`. **When a check indicts a name your PR never wrote, run it on the base.**

With the fix `nsslice` reports **0 rows** for this PR — `LinearEquiv` is rooted completely, all 8
declarations across both files. The failure had been pure noise.

### Controls 94 → 97, and the tally caught my own insertion bug
Three new controls (positive: reports the namespace THIS PR half-roots; negative: silent about one
`main` had already rooted; regression: the un-based path still shows the false positive). Two
mistakes, both caught by the suite rather than by me:

1. I inserted the block **after** `p=$(grep -c P "$RES")`, so the three PASS lines printed and the
   total stayed at 94. **A control that prints PASS but is not counted is r237 again** — the suite says
   so in its own comments. Moved above the tally; total went 94 → 97.
2. Renaming the fixture variable off the colliding `NB` missed `cp -R "$NB/."`, so the new control
   copied the r551 fixture and two checks went red. The red was correct.

`api-design` asked to publish `Module.End.{prodMap_pow, aeval_prodMap}` (both `private`, both general
and stated wholly in Mathlib's API) and to mark them and `Module.End.{rTensorAlgHom_apply,
lTensorAlgHom_apply}` `@[simp]`. Implemented all four in `a260a2ac25`, gate 12 ok / 0 failed.

> **Publishing a declaration costs a docstring.** `lint-env` documents all 8441 public declarations
> (`0 undocumented`), so `private` → public without a `/-- … -/` fails the build. Both got one.

The three new `@[simp]` tags are the #6093 risk again, and CI is the adjudicator — `simpNF` rejected

`7b0b2e546f`, 8 declarations, 2 files, lint **792 → 784**, gate **10 ok / 2 failed**. Both failures are

## r593 — the same defect a third time, found by looking for it instead of tripping over it

**Round outcome: `tool-fix`.** merged=0. open=3. Nothing was actionable (#6113 re-drive not eligible
until 08:12Z, board BEHIND so no re-fix; #6093 blocked on substance; #5950 human-gated).

### The class, stated
r551 `nsbalance` printed 4600 false rows on green `main`. r592 `nsslice` reported a namespace `main`
had already rooted. Both were the same mistake: **a check that describes the absolute state of a file
is read by `prepush` as a description of the PR**, because `prepush` filters its rows to the changed
files. Twice is a coincidence; I went looking for the third.

### `parallelns` had it: 24 rows on green `main`
```
$ parallelns.py <pristine snapshot of main> --mathlib …   ->  24 rows
[SAME Submodule: rooted 1 / nested 4  …] TauCeti/Algebra/Module/Lattice.lean
    rooted: Submodule (1)
    still nested: LinearEquiv (4), Submodule (4), Submodule.IsLattice (1), TensorProduct (8)
```
That is byte-for-byte the row r592's `LinearEquiv` PR was blamed for. **207 files on `main` carry a
pre-existing `_root_.` declaration**, and 24 of them already produce a row — each a landmine for any
PR that opens the file for an unrelated reason. Fixed with `--base <ref>`, wired into `prepush.sh`.

### Suppressing on the row TEXT was not enough — suppress on the CLAIM
The first cut compared whole rows and **still fired** on `Lattice.lean`: rooting `LinearEquiv` removes
it from the nested list, so the row text legitimately changed. But the row's only assertion is the
`[SAME Submodule: rooted 1 / nested 4]` balance, and my PR moved none of it.

> **A row is its claim, not its rendering.** Suppress on `{k: (rooted, nested) for k in SAME}` — the
> namespaces the tag is actually about. Comparing the text makes the delta as noisy as the absolute
> scan for any PR that touches a flagged file at all. With the claim-level comparison: **24 suppressed,
> 0 remaining.**

The control pins both directions, which is what makes it worth having: root an *unrelated* namespace
in the file → silent; root one of the four nested `Submodule` theorems → fires, because that is the
claim changing. Controls **97 → 100**.

### What the gate says now
`improve/linearequiv-root`: **11 ok, 1 failed** (was 10/2). The survivor is `slice` —
*"rooted 4 of 12 flagged"* — which is **accurate**: this PR really does root 4 of that file's 12, and
the r512 question deserves the body answer, not a tool fix. `improve/iscompactoperator-root` re-gated
clean at 12 ok / 0 failed, so the change suppresses rows without loosening anything.

> **Audit note for the remaining checks.** `siblingscan`, `importcover`, `xsibling` and `deadpath` have
> not been proven delta-correct. The test is one command and costs nothing: **run the check against a
> pristine snapshot of `main`.** If it produces rows there, `prepush` will blame them on whoever next
> touches those files. Do this the moment one of them fires on a name the diff does not contain.

### A self-inflicted lesson worth keeping
My first patch appended the new docstring paragraph *after* the module docstring's closing `"""`,
turning prose into code (`SyntaxError: unterminated string literal`). I had a `.bak` and lost nothing.
**Anchor a docstring insertion on the closing quotes, not on the import that follows them.**

## r594 — finished the audit I promised; `deadpath` was the fourth, and the worst

**Round outcome: `tool-fix`.** merged=0. open=3. #6113 re-drive not eligible until 08:12Z (round ran
07:36–07:45Z), board BEHIND so no re-fix. Nothing else actionable.

### The audit, completed rather than deferred
r593 left a note: `siblingscan`, `importcover`, `xsibling`, `deadpath` unproven, test them when one
next fires. Waiting for a failure is the wrong trigger — the test is one command. Reading the call
sites settled two immediately:

| check | call in `prepush.sh` | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `importcover` | builds `$WORK` and diffs `head_rows` vs `base_rows` | **already a delta** ✓ |
| `xsibling` | passed `$(git merge-base "$BASE" HEAD)` | **already takes a base** ✓ |
| `siblingscan` | driven per removed wrapper, scoped by the PR's own edits | fine in practice |
| `deadpath` | `deadpath.py TauCeti "$ML" $CHANGED` — **no base** | 🔴 **defective** |

### `deadpath` blames the file, and most of the tree is a file
```
250-file sample of an older main : 95 rows across 33 files
                                   (Vandermonde 15, EulerCharacteristic 14, Northcott 8)
250-file sample of TODAY's main  : 11 rows across  5 files
```
`prepush` prints *"every qualified name **this PR writes** resolves"*, but the scan is absolute: a
reference already dead in a file is charged to whoever next opens it. It had not bitten me only
because my changed files happened to miss the affected ones — a latent landmine, not a quiet tool.
Fixed with `--base <ref>`: a row is dropped when its token already appears in that file at the base.
Verified on a real file — `RepresentationTheory/AsModule.lean`, untouched, 3 rows → **3 suppressed, 0**.

> **A declaration this PR DELETED out from under a live reference is `stalequal`'s row, not this
> one.** The two halves stay disjoint, so scoping `deadpath` to the delta loses no coverage.

### Four instances, one sentence
**r551 `nsbalance`, r592 `nsslice`, r593 `parallelns`, r594 `deadpath`: a check that describes a
file's absolute state is read by `prepush` as a description of the PR, because `prepush` filters its
rows to the changed files.** Every gate check is now either delta-scoped or proven not to need it.

### Three fixture mistakes, each caught by the control failing
The negative control passed immediately and both positives failed — the fixture was producing no rows
at all. In order:
1. **Dead name in a docstring.** `deadpath`'s DEAD-PATH half *masks comments* (its DEAD-NS half does
   not). Prose fixtures test the other half.
2. **Nothing rooted into `Gone`.** `deadpath` only checks tokens whose head is a namespace the tree
   roots into, so `Gone.vanished_lemma` was never a candidate. r552's fixture pins this with a
   `theorem _root_.Wrap.anchor`; mine needed `_root_.Gone.anchor`.
3. `$MLFIX` undefined — the fixture had no Mathlib dir, and `deadpath` UNRUNs on an empty index
   rather than calling every name dead (r552's own guard, working).

> **A control that fails while the tool is right is the fixture being wrong, and it is worth the four
> minutes.** Had I written only the negative, it would have passed against a fixture that generates
> nothing and pinned exactly nothing.

Controls **100 → 103**. Gate re-run on `improve/linearequiv-root`: **11 ok, 1 failed**, unchanged —
the surviving `slice` row is accurate and belongs in the PR body.

### zsh, again
`files=$(find …)` then `deadpath … $files` passed **one argument containing every path**; zsh does not
word-split unquoted `$var`. The tool's own UNRUN guard caught it by reporting a target named
`TauCeti/Order` that does not exist. Use `files=("${(@f)$(…)}")` and `"${files[@]}"`.

## r595 — I "corrected" a number with a worse one; a name is not a declaration

**Round outcome: `corrected`.** merged=0. open=3. #6113 eligible at 08:12Z; round ran 07:51–07:55Z.

### The error
For three rounds I argued #6093's `generality` fix was too big for this PR, at "**47 references across
8 files**". In r589 I re-measured, got "**~150 across 13**", posted it to the reviewer *as a correction
of my own understatement*, and recorded the lesson as *"measure the argument you are already making"*.

The second number was worse than the first. I had counted `\bfiberMap\b` across `TauCeti/` **without
checking the matches were one declaration.** There are two:

| declaration | site | family |
|---|---|---|
| `ContinuousMap.fiberMap` | `Topology/Homotopy/Monodromy/Functoriality.lean:56` | the one under review |
| **`Deck.fiberMap`** | `AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Deck/Fiber/Transport.lean:52` | `@[expose] def`, own `_apply_coe`, `_symm_apply_coe`, `_refl`, `_symm` |

Every heavy row in the table I published was the **second**: `Transport.lean` (78),
`TorsorTransport.lean` (50), `SubgroupFiberOrbit/Basic.lean` (22), `Orbit.lean` (12). **None of them
reference `ContinuousMap.fiberMap` at all.** The tell was in my own output and I read past it:
`98 fiberMap / 24 ContinuousMap.fiberMap / 1 TauCeti.Deck.fiberMap` — a second qualified spelling
sitting in the frequency table.

### The true scope
```
ContinuousMap.fiberMap   34 refs / 8 files   (13 inside Functoriality.lean itself => 21 external / 7 files)
compFiberEquiv           13 refs / 1 file    -- ENTIRELY LOCAL, zero external references
```
`compFiberEquiv` → `Equiv.compFiberEquiv` is a **one-file** change. The whole job is an ordinary PR.

### The lesson, and why it is not the one I recorded in r589
r589's lesson — *"measure the argument you are already making"* — was right and I obeyed it. It did
not save me, because I measured the wrong thing more carefully. The missing step is upstream:

> **A NAME IS NOT A DECLARATION.** Before counting references to `X`, establish how many declarations
> are called `X`. `grep -rhoE '[A-Za-z0-9_.]*\bX\b' | sort | uniq -c` costs one command and prints the
> qualified spellings; two roots in that table means two declarations and a conflated count.

This is `mathlibns` (r511) in a different suit: a grep answers *"does this string occur"* and I keep
reading it as *"does this thing exist"*.

### Posted the correction unprompted
On the `generality` thread, stating plainly that I over-corrected, that the size argument I leaned on
is gone, and that the work still belongs in its own PR under "One topic per PR" — **with no request**,
since the finding is accepted and re-litigating it would be the second error.

> Correcting a number *downward* is harder to volunteer than upward: it removes an argument I had been
> winning on. That is exactly why it had to be volunteered.

### What this changes
The generalisation is no longer the risky cross-cutting job I described to Chris. **~34 references,
8 files, one half confined to a single file, with the `Deck/` mass entirely out of scope.** The
blocker I cited — 150 blind references at ~13 min per CI cycle — was an artefact of my own bad count.
Recommendation upgraded from "ask before starting" to **"do it next, when a slot frees"**.

|---|---|---|

## r597 — measured the prerequisite properly; the count was never the problem

**Round outcome: `measured`.** merged=0. open=3. #6113 re-drive not eligible until ~09:45Z.
`reuse` contest unanswered (inert until driven). **#6093's board was refreshed by `ldct`** — a third
party, not me and not a local worker — and now reads `api-design` + `generality` + `placement`
blocking, 7 green. Still blocked on substance; left alone.

### My original number was right, and the "correction" was the error
Applying r595's rule *before* counting this time — `grep -rhoE '[A-Za-z0-9_.]*\bfiberMap\b' | uniq -c`
prints the qualified spellings, and two roots mean two declarations:

```
main:  111 fiberMap · 10 IsCoveringMap.fiberMap · 3 TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.fiberMap
         1 TauCeti.Deck.fiberMap · 1 Deck.fiberMap
```
Classified by file: **COVER 47 refs / 9 files** (the family under review) and **DECK 170 refs /
5 files** (an unrelated `@[expose] def`, entirely out of scope). So the true figure is **47 / 9** —
which is what I said in the first place, before "correcting" it to ~150 / 13 in r589 and correcting
that again in r595. Three measurements, and the first was the good one.

### The half I assumed was trivial is not separable
On `main` the equivalence is **`homeomorphCompFiberEquiv`**; `compFiberEquiv` does not exist there at
all — **#6093 is what renames it**, moving `homeomorph` out of the identifier and into the receiver.
So `generality`'s second bullet cannot be done on `main` first: generalising a declaration *called*
`homeomorphCompFiberEquiv` to accept an `Equiv` makes its own name a lie. **That half is gated on
#6093's rename**, which fixes the sequencing question I had been asking Chris to answer in the
abstract.

### 🔴 And the count was never what made it hard
The change is **not uniform**. `fiberMap_monodromy` genuinely needs continuity — it builds
`q' : C(F, X)` and `q'.comp f` — so it must KEEP `f : C(E, F)` and call the generalised `fiberMap ⇑f`.
Every external call site then needs a coercion inserted, and they look like this:

```
Monodromy/Basic.lean:129    (IsCoveringMap.fiberMap_apply_coe f.hom.left.hom (proj_hom_comp_hom_left_hom f) …
ActionCover.lean:194        rw [TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.fiberMap_apply_coe, actionCov…
Existence.lean:167          rw [TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.fiberMap_apply_coe]
```

They pass **bundled** maps (`f.hom.left.hom`, `ι`, `actionCoverTotalSpace…` — morphisms in a category
of covers) from inside `rw` and `simpa only [...]` chains. **Inserting `⇑` changes the term shape the
rewrite matches on.** That is the failure mode a typechecker catches in seconds and a 13-minute CI
cycle catches one site at a time.

> **The reference count measured the wrong axis.** I upgraded my recommendation to "do it next" on the
> strength of 34-vs-150; the number was never the obstacle. **Ask what the call sites LOOK like, not
> just how many there are** — 40 coercion insertions inside proof scripts is a different job from 40
> in ordinary term position, and only reading them tells you which you have.

### Did not start it, and that is the point
With ~50 minutes and no way to typecheck, beginning a 47-site coercion refactor ends the round with a
half-finished branch and no verdict. Deleted the empty scratch branch.

**This is the first time the broken Mathlib cache has blocked real work rather than merely slowed it.**
Every other change this session was checkable by a static gate plus one CI cycle. This one is not.

## r598 — `rootns <tail>` rooted three declarations into a namespace that does not exist, and said "3 rooted"

**Round outcome: `target dropped + tool gap found`.** merged=0. open=3. #6113 not eligible until
~09:45Z. Probed the r591 survey's #2 target and it failed — for a reason I did not predict.

### The near-miss
`SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData` is 2/2 WHOLE and `mathlibns` verified it **ROOT 6**. I ran

```
rootns.py LocalGeneratorsData  …/Invertible/Basic.lean
# FIRING CONTROL: 3 declaration(s) rooted into `LocalGeneratorsData` across 1 file(s)
```

Success-shaped, and **wrong**. The file's shape is

```lean
namespace TauCeti
namespace SheafOfModules                                   -- line 50
structure LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible (q : …) …       -- dotted head
def       LocalGeneratorsData.ofIso        (q : …) …
```

so the namespace to root is **split**: `SheafOfModules` comes from the *wrapper*, `LocalGeneratorsData`
from the *declaration's dotted head*. Passing the tail rooted them to `_root_.LocalGeneratorsData.*`,
**dropping `SheafOfModules`** — a namespace `mathlibns` never blessed and Mathlib does not have. Passing
the correct compound `SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData` matches **0** declarations, because `rootns`
looks for the whole name in one place.

Only the gate caught it: `decldiff` (4 VANISHED with no rooting to explain them), `stalequal` (a live
external reference at `WeilDivisor/Scheme/Invertible.lean:149`), and decisively
**`lint-dot-notation: NEW violations`** — the extraction *created* lint findings. **7 ok, 5 failed.**

### I predicted the wrong failure
I reasoned from r515 that `nsslice` would fire, because `LocalTriviality.lean` carries
`namespace LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible` — that class's own API in another file. **`nsslice`
passed.** Every failure was something else. The inference was plausible, well-grounded in a real
past defect, and simply not what happened.

> **Running the gate is cheaper than predicting it, and it is not the same activity.** I have spent
> several rounds fixing checks that fire wrongly; the corollary is that when they fire *rightly* they
> know things I do not. Probe first, theorise after.

### The tool gap, and why the survey cannot see it
`nscand` reports the namespace by its **full path** (`SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData`) and
`mathlibns` verifies that path — but `rootns` takes a namespace that must sit either wholly in the
wrapper or wholly in the dotted head. **A split namespace has no correct argument.** The dangerous
half is that the wrong argument does not error: it roots to a shorter namespace and reports the count.

**Next tool task** (not started, ~13 min was not enough to do it with a control): teach `rootns` to
accept a namespace that spans wrapper *and* dotted head, and — cheaper and independently worth doing —
make its firing control **print the resulting full names**, so rooting into the wrong namespace is
visible in the output instead of only in the gate three steps later.

### `LocalGeneratorsData` — dropped for now
Not because it is a bad target, but because it cannot be extracted correctly with today's `rootns`.
Re-test it after the tool is fixed. The r515 subtree caveat (4 files, `IsInvertible` and
`IsLocallyFreeData` APIs spread across them) remains a separate open question about the target itself.

## r599 — the contradiction resolved against me, which is the outcome a real contest has to allow

**Round outcome: `resolved`.** merged=0. open=3. #6113 head `694ee7e8fc`, CI green 15:22:54Z.

### A review can hang, and the process being alive is not the tell
The run I launched at 09:45 was still alive at 11:51 — **2h06m**, against a normal ~8 minutes — with
its log **last written at 10:45**. It had got as far as `author replies on threads: reuse×1`, so it
saw the contest, and then stalled in the per-rubric phase. `pkill -f` did not take; `kill -TERM` by
PID did.

> **The liveness signal is the log's mtime, not `pgrep`.** A hung run looks exactly like a working one
> to a process check, and I polled it twice on that basis. Check `ls -l` on the output before assuming
> a long run is merely slow.

Also: other workers on this box were mid-review on **6035, 6117, 6124, 6125**. Kill by **PID**, never
`pkill -f tauceti-review`, or you take down somebody else's session.

### `generality` cleared; `reuse` was answered against me
`ldct` — a third party, not me and not a local worker — posted an on-head board at 12:37. The
`CommSemiring` fix worked: **`generality` green**. And the contest answer:

> re-reviewed on `0cf0d1a`; **the finding stands** — The refactor unnecessarily promotes two private
> proof helpers into public specialization lemmas already derivable from generic Mathlib API.

So the `api-design` ↔ `reuse` contradiction resolved **in favour of `private`** — against the change I
had made. `694ee7e8fc` does exactly what I said in the contest I would do: both back to

## r600 — fixed the r598 near-miss: the rooted name now comes from the declaration, not the argument

**Round outcome: `tool-fix`.** merged=0 (newest still #6082). open=3. #6113 re-drive eligible ~16:23Z.

### The defect
Both of `rootns`'s rewrite paths built the new name out of the **namespace argument**:

```python
if i in inblock:                 new = f"_root_.{NS}.{name}"      # bare name inside `namespace NS`
elif name.startswith(NS + '.'):  new = f"_root_.{name}"           # dotted name
```

Neither looks at what encloses the declaration, so **any wrapper between `TauCeti` and the target is
dropped**. `Invertible/Basic.lean` opens `namespace TauCeti` then `namespace SheafOfModules` and writes
`structure LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible` dotted; r598's `rootns LocalGeneratorsData` produced
`_root_.LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible` — a namespace Mathlib does not have — and reported
`3 declaration(s) rooted`.

### The fix is one sentence
**The rooted name is the declaration's own full name minus a leading `TauCeti`.** Computed from
`scopes()` at the declaration's line, so it is right whatever the argument selected:

```
rootns LocalGeneratorsData                  -> _root_.SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible
rootns SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData   -> _root_.SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible
```

Both now land in the namespace `mathlibns` verified (**ROOT 6**). A compound argument — which is what
`nscand` and `mathlibns` both *print* — selects the same declarations as its tail, so the name you are
handed by the survey is now a name the tool accepts. Regression-checked against the `LinearEquiv`
extraction: 8 declarations, same 12/12 diff as the staged branch.

### The firing control now prints where things LANDED
Counting was never going to catch this: rooting to the wrong namespace **is** success-shaped, editing
declarations and returning a nonzero count. So it prints every resulting name and the set of landing
namespaces, with an instruction to check them against `mathlibns`:

```
ROOTED   _root_.SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible
# FIRING CONTROL: 3 declaration(s) rooted … landing in 1 namespace(s): SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData
```

> **r184 says a zero must be interpretable. r600 adds: so must a nonzero.** The count answered "did it
> do something"; the question was "did it do the right thing", and only the resulting names answer that.

### The suite caught my own regression, which is the whole point of having it
Changing `process()` to return a fourth value left the early-return path — the anonymous-instance
refusal — returning a 3-tuple, so `main()` raised on unpack. **`rootns: refuses a block holding an
anonymous instance` went red**, and I would not have thought to re-test the refusal path after an
unrelated signature change. Controls **103 → 107**, all green.

### #6113 unchanged this round
Another worker ran a review 15:30–15:38; it did **not** advance the board, which is still for
`0cf0d1ad49` while the head is `694ee7e8fc` (the `private` revert, CI green 15:22:54Z). I did not drive
alongside a live run. Re-drive at ~16:23Z.

## r601 — #6113 reaches 10/10; and I had been reading the wrong scoreboard comment for rounds

**Round outcome: `ready-to-merge + tool-fix`.** merged=0 yet. open=3.

### 🔴 My sweep was reading a STALE board — an instruction I had and did not follow
The standing prompt says: *read the `tauceti-meta:v1` scoreboard **sorted by updated_at***. I had been
taking `[...]|.[-1]` of the comment list, which is **creation** order. #6113 has **two** scoreboard
comments, and the live one was **created first, updated last**:

```
id=5597459108  created 06:51:43Z  updated 16:33:14Z   <- the real board, positionally FIRST
```

The pipeline **edits an existing comment** rather than always appending, so positional-last is simply
the wrong comment. This made me report #6113 as `BEHIND` in r600 and again this round when its board
was current, and it is why "another worker's review did not advance the board" (r600) was wrong — it
had advanced it. Correct query:

```
'[.[]|select(.body|test("kind\\":\\"scoreboard\\""))]|sort_by(.updated_at)|.[-1].body'
```

> **The instruction contained the fix and I read past it.** Every board I have quoted this session came
> through the bad query; re-checked #6093 (3 blocking / 7 green) and #5950 (10 green) with the correct
> one and they agree, so only #6113's recent rounds were affected. `sort_by(.updated_at)` from now on.

### #6113 — `reuse` approved, **10/10 green, `ready-to-merge`**
The drive at 16:23 scored `694ee7e8fc` and cleared the last rubric. The `api-design` ↔ `reuse`
contradiction is settled: contested, answered "keep private", reverted, and now both are green on the
same head. Five files, all under `TauCeti/`, so it satisfies the auto-merge path filter.

### A SECOND `rootns` gap: rooting a namespace must take its children
With r600's fix, `SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData` extracted correctly — but only 4 declarations.
`LocalTriviality.lean` opens `namespace LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible`, and block selection matched
only the namespace *itself*, so that child's API stayed nested while its parent went to the root —
**the r515 split, produced by the tool meant to avoid it.** Selection now accepts a child namespace of
the target. Controls **107, still green**, including the four r600 ones.

With the whole subtree moved (6 declarations, 3 files) the gate went **8 ok/4 failed → 11 ok/1**, and
`nsslice` — which fired correctly on the partial move — passes. That is the check doing exactly its job
in both directions within one round.

### `git checkout -B <branch> <start>` does NOT discard working-tree changes
I have been using it as the guardrail-safe discard pattern. It moves the branch pointer and **keeps
local modifications** when they do not conflict. Two extractions silently accumulated in one tree; the
result was correct only by luck, and the firing control's "2 rooted across 1 file" looked like a
regression when it was reporting only the *new* edits. **To discard, copy the file aside and `cp` it
back, or commit to a throwaway branch first.**

`--state merged --limit 400` returns the **400 most recent** merged PRs channel-wide, so older
`improve/*` merges fall out of the window as the channel merges anything at all. The count went
**51 → 49 across a round in which one of mine merged**, which is the tell: a number that drops when
you gain is not a total.

> Every merge figure I have quoted this session — 51, 59, 125 — was windowed or over-matched, and I
> relabelled it "all-time" without checking that the window covered all of it. **The count that is
> actually stable is the newest merged number** (#6113 now), and that is what the sweep should track.
> To get a true total, page `--search 'is:merged head:improve/'` to exhaustion, or stop claiming one.

## r605 — built the check that would have caught r604, and it immediately found surplus in two staged branches

**Round outcome: `fixed + new gate check`.** merged=0. open=3. Gate is now **13 checks**;
controls **107 → 110**.

### #6148's `api-design` fix shipped
Dropped the `_root_.IsCompactOperator.` prefix from the six unflagged private helpers (6 declaration
sites, 7 references). The PR now roots **exactly the 11 declarations the linter flags**. `decldiff`
correctly reports six paired VANISHED/APPEARED — `TauCeti.IsCompactOperator.x` → `TauCeti.x` is a
rename, not a rooting — and that is answered in the PR body rather than suppressed.

> **`decldiff` assumes a rooting PR only ever roots.** A PR asked by review to *stop* rooting
> something produces paired residue that is correct. Worth teaching it to recognise a de-rooting;
> for now the honest answer goes in the body.

### 🔧 `rootsurplus` — the question no check was asking
`rootns` moves a whole `namespace` block, so a PR roots every member of the wrapper rather than the
subset the linter flagged. **None of the twelve existing checks notices**, because `slice`,
`decldiff` and `nsslice` are all *satisfied* by rooting too much. New check, wired into the gate:

```
rootsurplus.py --base <ref> <flagged-file> <file.lean>...
   newly-rooted(HEAD) − newly-rooted(base)  ∖  flagged-at-base
```

**Injection-tested against the real case**: run on #6148's previous head `c48b396937` it reports
`17 newly rooted, 6 of them NOT flagged` and names exactly the six `api-design` found. On the fixed
head: `11 newly rooted, 0 not flagged`. Three controls (positive, negative, and UNRUN on an empty
flagged set, so it cannot call everything surplus).

### It found surplus in two of three staged branches — and both are *legitimate*
| branch | newly rooted | surplus | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `linearequiv` | 8 | **0** | clean |
| `subring` | 12 | **3** | deliberate — 2 private helpers cannot stay behind when the wrapper retires; `toAddSubgroup_closure_of_one_mem_of_mul_mem` is public and stranding it fires `nsslice` |
| `localgeneratorsdata` | 6 | **4** | deliberate — the `IsInvertible` child API, taken together precisely so one class is not split (r601) |

Both are already explained in their commit messages. **That is the check working as intended**: a
surplus is not a defect, it is *a claim the PR makes on its own authority*, and the difference between
these and #6148's six is that these were decisions and those were an accident I never saw. The check
converts an invisible accident into a visible decision.

> Three checks passing is not the same as the question being asked. `slice`, `decldiff` and `nsslice`
> were all green on #6148 while it rooted six declarations nobody requested. **When a reviewer finds
> something the gate missed, the useful response is to ask which question the gate never posed** —
> not to add a special case for the instance.

### `documentation` on #6148 — contested, and the numbers matter
Asked to delete roadmap "Lane" sentences from two module docstrings. This PR **does not edit either
sentence** (its diff to those files is `TauCeti.`-prefix removal plus `namespace` → `section`), and
**169 files on main carry the same convention**. Removing two would make the codebase less consistent.
Offered to do it repo-wide as its own PR. I had made the edit before counting, and reverted it once I
had — **check the convention before you "fix" two instances of it.**

## r606 — `decldiff` was telling the truth about the wrong thing

**Round outcome: `tool-fix`.** merged=0. open=3. #6148's `api-design` fix built **green 19:11:50Z** on
`224caa567a`; re-drive eligible ~20:12Z. Controls **110 → 112**.

### The message was false, not merely noisy
r605 left #6148 failing `decldiff` with twelve rows saying *"no rooting explains it"* for six paired
changes. A rooting did not explain them — **a de-rooting did, exactly.** The check pairs
`TauCeti.X.y` removed ↔ `X.y` added and knows no other shape, so the reverse rename
(`TauCeti.NS.y` → `TauCeti.y`) fell through into residue.

That is worth separating from the r592–r594 family. Those checks fired on things that were **not this
PR's doing**. This one fired on something the PR *did* do — it simply described it wrongly. **A check
can be right to fire and wrong about why**, and the second failure is the one that wastes a reviewer's
time, because the operator cannot tell a mislabelled row from a real one.

Now: `11 rooted as intended; 6 DE-ROOTED the other way; 0 VANISHED and 0 APPEARED`, and the gate's
heading reads *"the declaration set changed by more than a rooting"* rather than the old claim.

### Still blocking, deliberately
A de-rooting drops a namespace level from the declaration set and belongs in the PR body. The fix
changes what the operator is **told**, not whether they must answer. The r550 precedent for
non-blocking rows (TACTIC/ATTRIBUTE in `xsibling`) did not apply: those are references, this is the
declaration set.

### The control that mattered was the one I did not add
Two decldiff controls already existed, and the important result was that **both still pass** — in
particular *"a rename that is not a rooting leaves residue"*, which uses the r564 fixture's
`map_injective` rename. Had de-rooting recognition been written loosely (pair any removed name with
any added name sharing a leaf), that control would have gone red. It did not.

> My first attempt at the new control reused the r564 fixture with a `sed` for a declaration that
> **does not exist in it** — the substitution silently did nothing and the `neg` assertion would have
> passed vacuously, testing nothing at all. Caught it by checking the fixture before trusting the
> PASS. **A negative control on a fixture that cannot produce the thing is worse than no control**,
> because it reads as evidence.

### Gate and suite
13 checks; #6148 now **12 ok / 1 failed**, the failure being the six labelled DE-ROOTED rows.
`rootsurplus` (r605) reports `every rooted declaration was flagged` — the defect that started this
sequence is closed and now guarded.

## r607 — read #6093's findings instead of assuming them; all three are one refactor

**Round outcome: `answered`.** merged=0. open=3. #6148 re-drive eligible ~20:12Z.

### I had been assuming, not reading
`ldct` refreshed #6093's board at 08:28 and I recorded "3 blocking, same as before, leave alone" for
several rounds without opening the findings. Reading them changed the picture: they are **not** three
independent objections but one refactor seen from three rubrics.

| rubric | asks | status |
|---|---|---|
| `generality` | restate `fiberMap` for `f : E → F` (under `Function`), `compFiberEquiv` for `h : X ≃ Y` | accepted r589; cache-blocked |
| `placement` | move both families out of the monodromy module into a generic one | accepted this round |
| `api-design` | `@[simp]` on `fiberMap_comp_apply` and `monodromyNatTrans_comp` | **already disproved by `simpNF`** |

**The order is forced**: restate at the natural level, *then* place the result. Moving first relocates
signatures that are about to change, and the destination depends on the outcome — a construction
taking `f : E → F` is not a *topology* file's business at all. Done backwards it is two moves and two
rounds of import rewiring. Said so on the `placement` thread rather than leaving a future round to
discover it.

### `api-design` is downstream of `generality`, which is the useful part
It re-fired asking for the two `@[simp]` tags that `lint-env` rejected in r589 — LHS not in simp normal
form, because the composite's compatibility proof is an **inline term** (`fiberMap (g.comp f) (by
funext z; …)`). Replied with the linter output again, and with the connection I had not previously
drawn: **under `generality`'s signature the composite becomes `g ∘ f` and the proof can be a
parameter**, which may put the LHS in normal form and make the annotation valid.

> So the right answer to `api-design` is not "no", it is "not yet, and here is what would change it".
> Three findings that each looked like a separate cost are one piece of work whose parts unlock each
> other — and I only saw that by reading all three together instead of triaging them one at a time.

### Did not drive
The contest is inert until someone reviews, but driving would re-roll the board (r589) without
unblocking anything: `generality` stands, accepted, and is gated on the cache. #6093's board is
already on head, so the standing re-drive condition is not met either. The replies sit on the record;
a full review picks up author replies automatically (`author replies on threads: …` in the run log).

## r609 — restructured #6148 so it stops touching what nobody flagged; a red build corrected me on r389

**Round outcome: `restructured, CI green`.** merged=0. open=3. #6148 head `ddc3afb3ff`, gate
**13 ok / 0 failed**, CI **green 21:18:45Z**. `documentation` on #6148 **cleared** — the contest held.

### The better answer to a scope disagreement is to remove the disagreement
`api-design` re-fired asking for the half I had declined: relocate and *export* the six private
helpers into canonical modules. Rather than contest scope a second time, I made the PR stop touching
them: `Eigenspace.lean` and `RieszTheory.lean` now **keep** their `namespace IsCompactOperator`
wrapper, because those six live in it, and only the flagged declarations are written
`_root_.IsCompactOperator.…`. **All six are byte-identical to `main` — 0 diff lines each.** The PR
roots exactly the 11 declarations the linter flags, down from 17.

> Contesting was available and would probably have worked. Restructuring was better because it makes
> the remaining half of the finding true *about `main`* rather than about this PR — the same move that
> cleared `documentation`. **Check whether you can stop touching the thing before arguing about it.**

### 🔴 A red build corrected my reading of r389
I asserted that keeping the wrapper keeps rooted siblings reachable by short name. **It does not**, and
CI said so: `Eigenspace.lean:135: Unknown identifier finiteDimensional_eigenspace`.

r389's rule is about `namespace Foo` **at root**. Here the wrapper opens `TauCeti.IsCompactOperator`,
while rooting moves the declaration to `IsCompactOperator` — a *different* namespace that the wrapper
does not open. Lean tries `TauCeti.IsCompactOperator.x`, `TauCeti.x`, then root `x`; it never tries
`IsCompactOperator.x`. So the references needed qualifying exactly as they would have if the wrapper
had gone. Twelve of them, then wrapped; gate clean; CI green.

> **I cited a ledger rule instead of checking it.** The rule was real and its precondition was not
> met. `settle` could not catch it either — `xsibling` models breakage caused by a wrapper being
> *removed*, and here the wrapper stayed while the declaration left. A shape none of the tooling had
> seen, because until now rooting always retired the wrapper.

### `siblingscan` was per-namespace where the removal is per-file
It reported `Eigenspace.lean` and `RieszTheory.lean` as broken by "removing `namespace
IsCompactOperator`" — a wrapper both files **keep**. `prepush` collected removed `namespace` lines from
the **whole diff** and then scanned every changed file for each name, so `Basic.lean`'s genuine removal
was attributed to two files that still have it. Now computed per file, and a wrapper still present at
HEAD is not treated as removed.

### Answering "have you forgotten any?"
Checked rather than assumed. **50 PRs repo-wide are `awaiting-author`; exactly one is mine**: #6093,
tracked. The other CBirkbeck rows are `adic/`, `chebotarev/`, `elliptic/`, `modular/` and `docs/` —
other workers on the shared account, outside this remit (#5481 explicitly so). All **3** open
`improve/*` PRs are tracked: #6148 `awaiting-review`, #6093 `awaiting-author`, #5950 `ready-to-merge`.

**But the fork carries ~97 `improve/*` branches with no PR ever opened.** The four newest are this
session's deliberate staging (`localgeneratorsdata`, `subring`, `linearequiv`) plus `alghom-root`,
dropped with cause in r580. **The other ~93 all date from Sept 4–5**, before this session's rounds, and
I do not know whether they are abandoned or lost work — main has moved hundreds of commits since, so
each would need a rebase and a re-gate to find out. Flagged for Chris rather than guessed at.

## r610 — Chris was right: there IS forgotten work, and it is not among the open PRs

**Round outcome: `triaged`.** merged=0. open=3. #6148 re-drive eligible ~22:19Z.

### The check he asked for, and what it actually found
Open PRs were fine — 50 repo-wide are `awaiting-author`, exactly **one** is mine (#6093, tracked), and
all 3 open `improve/*` are accounted for. **The gap is in branches that were never opened at all.**

```
97 improve/* fork branches with no PR
├── 71 still merge CLEAN onto today's main
│   ├──  4 deliberate: this session's staged trio + alghom-root (dropped with cause, r580)
│   └── 67 from Sept 4-5, before this session
└── 26 CONFLICT (stale)
```

Of the 67, **16 have zero mentions in this ledger** — they are not dropped-with-cause, they are
unrecorded. Saved the full classification to `unopened-branches-r610.tsv`.

### Sampled three, and they are real finished work
- `idealcount-drop-unused-primality` — drops `hQ : Q.IsPrime` and `hQ0 : Q ≠ ⊥` from a private
  theorem, renames it to a conclusion-accurate name, and documents **why** the hypotheses are
  unnecessary. One file, 7/8 lines. Applies cleanly. This is exactly the `generality` improvement the
  rubrics ask for.
- `cluster-set-forward-inclusion` — docstring restructuring, one file, 91/79 lines.
- `narrow-unit-norm-one` — drops a redundant nonzeroness hypothesis, states a `-1` companion beside
  its `+1` sibling. Two files.

All three have proper commit messages and coherent scope. **They look finished and were never opened.**

### The failure was in my own bookkeeping, not the board
Every sweep this session asked *"which of my PRs need work?"* and never *"which of my finished work
never became a PR?"* The 3-slot rule makes staging normal, so an unopened branch is indistinguishable
from a deliberately-parked one **unless the ledger says which** — and for 16 of them it says nothing.

> **A queue discipline that parks work needs a record of what is parked and why.** `last-round.md`
> tracks the three staged branches by name; it has never carried the other 94. The sweep should count
> unopened `improve/*` fork branches and flag any that are CLEAN and unrecorded — that is a one-line
> check I did not have because I only ever looked at PRs.

### Not opening any
Would breach the 3-slot rule, and each needs a rebase, a re-gate and a CI cycle before it is worth a
reviewer's time. **This is Chris's call**, and the data is on disk for whichever way he decides.

## r611 — correcting r610: I measured "has commits" and reported it as "is unlanded work"

**Round outcome: `corrected`.** merged=0. open=3. #6148 re-drive eligible ~22:19Z.

### The number I gave Chris was wrong, and wrong in the alarming direction
r610 reported **"67 forgotten branches that still apply"**. The real figure is **31**, and the
difference is a git incantation that does not mean what I read it as:

```
git diff --name-only origin/main...fork/$b      # THREE dots: the branch's own commits since it forked
                                                 # -- NON-EMPTY for every branch that has any commit
```

That answers *"did this branch ever change anything?"*, not *"does it still change anything?"* Every
one of the 97 scored LIVE because every one of them has commits. The question actually needed is
whether **applying the branch to today's main alters main**:

```
t=$(git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main fork/$b)
[ "$t" = "$(git rev-parse origin/main^{tree})" ] && echo SUPERSEDED
```

Corrected: **62 SUPERSEDED** (already in main), **35 LIVE**, **0 CONFLICT**. Four of the LIVE are this
session's deliberate staging, so **31 older branches genuinely still contribute** — under half of what
I reported. `unopened-branches-r611.tsv` replaces the r610 file, which I deleted rather than leave
sitting next to it looking authoritative.

### Two measurement errors in one round, both caught by trying to *use* the result
- `merge-tree` said `idealcount-drop-unused-primality` was CLEAN; **the rebase conflicted**. A merge
  and a rebase are different questions — a rebase replays each commit and can break on an
  intermediate state a merge never constructs. Since these PRs ship as one squashed commit, the
  revival path is `git merge --squash`, not `git rebase`.
- Squash-merging that branch then produced **an empty diff** — its work is already in `main`. The very
  branch I had sampled as proof of "real finished work" was the proof that my classification was broken.

> **Both errors survived a plausible-looking command and died the moment I ran the result.** The
> triage ran, printed, and got written up; it fell over on first contact with an actual rebase.
> This is r595's lesson in a new suit — I checked *how many*, never *of what* — and the fix is the
> same: **before reporting a measurement, use it once for the thing it is supposed to inform.**

### What still stands from r610
The structural point survives intact: **the sweep never asked which finished work never became a PR**,
and 3-slot staging makes a parked branch indistinguishable from an abandoned one unless the ledger
says which. That gap is real; only its size was overstated. 31 branches dating **2026-08-24 to
09-05** still contribute, and the ledger names few of them.

**Still Chris's call**, and now on an accurate number.

## r612 — audited my own claim on a review thread and found it overstated

**Round outcome: `corrected`.** merged=0. open=3. #6148 board now **ON-HEAD** (`ddc3afb3ff`),
9 green / `api-design` blocking. No re-drive needed — the board is current.

### The board caught up; my thread comment had not
A third party scored `ddc3afb3ff` at 21:44. My 20:48 reply on the `api-design` thread is still the
last word there — a fresh rubric run is **not** an answer to a contest — but two details of that reply
had gone stale, and I only found them by checking rather than assuming:

1. **The SHA.** I cited `48536a243f`. That push failed CI (the r609 r389 mistake) and the head is now
   `ddc3afb3ff`. A reviewer following the SHA would have landed on a red commit.
2. **"Zero diff lines each" was not true for one of the six.**
   `finiteDimensional_genEigenspace_nat_of_eigenspace` shows two diff lines — as a *call site* inside
   `finiteDimensional_genEigenspace_nat`, a rooted declaration whose line was rewrapped when its other
   argument gained a qualification. The declaration itself is untouched.

Posted both corrections with the exact diff hunk, and restated the claim in the form that actually
holds: **all six declarations are unchanged — names, namespace, privacy, statements, proofs** — and
none is declared, renamed, moved or re-scoped by this PR.

> **I have spent this session holding reviewers to precise claims.** "Zero diff lines each" was the
> kind of crisp, checkable overstatement I would have contested if a rubric made it — near enough to
> true to feel safe, and wrong on inspection. The asymmetry matters: a reviewer who checks it finds me
> imprecise on the one thing my whole argument rests on.

### The pattern across r610–r612
Three consecutive rounds of correcting my own numbers: 67 → 31 forgotten branches, merge-clean
mistaken for rebase-clean, and now "zero diff lines". Each survived because it was **plausible and
unchecked**, and each died on first contact with the thing it described. The measurements are getting
caught faster — r610's took a round, r612's took ten minutes — but the failure mode is one habit:
**stating a number I derived once and did not re-derive after the artefact changed.**

A SHA in a review comment is exactly that shape. **When a head moves, every claim quoting the old one
needs re-checking, not just the ones that look affected.**

## r615 — third correction of the same count: 67 → 31 → **5**

**Round outcome: `corrected`.** merged=0. open=3. #6148 still 10/10 `ready-to-merge` (merges cleanly,
9 behind main, `mergeable=UNKNOWN` is GitHub computing lazily) — waiting on the pipeline, not blocked.

### The count was wrong again, and for a third distinct reason
```
r610   67 forgotten   -- used `origin/main...branch` (THREE dots): the branch's own commits.
                         Non-empty for every branch that has any commit at all.
r611   31 forgotten   -- used `merge-tree --write-tree`, compared its output to main's tree.
                         But on CONFLICT that command prints the tree OID *plus the conflict
                         report* and exits NON-ZERO -- so every conflicting branch scored LIVE.
r615    5 forgotten   -- check the EXIT CODE; take only the first line as the tree.
```
Final: **62 SUPERSEDED, 26 CONFLICT, 9 LIVE** — and 4 of the LIVE are this session's own staged
branches. **Five older branches genuinely still apply.**

`r611` even printed **`CONFLICT: 0`** across 97 branches, which is not a plausible number for work
averaging two weeks old, and I wrote it up without blinking. Sampling five of its "LIVE" rows found
five conflicts.

### The five, all small and coherent
| branch | size | what |
|---|---|---|
| `nebentypus-ring-sibling-ref` | 1 file, +1/-1 | corrects a stale sibling-file doc reference |
| `levi-kernel-hcoe-golf` | 1 file, +2/-10 | proves the parabolic-point coercion bridge directly |
| `e6-minuscule-kostantform-reuse-v2` | 2 files, +18/-51 | reuses `rep_kostantForm_mem_lattice` instead of reproving |
| `riemann-roch-mul-pow-membership` | 1 file, +35/-30 | names the Riemann-Roch membership lemma |
| `coweight-refl-long-case` | 1 file, +44/-0 | **uncertain** — its tip is a merge of `main`, so the +44 may be a merge artefact |

### The habit, stated plainly
Three rounds, three wrong numbers, one cause: **I ran a command, read its output as if I knew its
contract, and reported the result.** Three dots vs two. Exit status vs stdout. Merge vs rebase. Each
time the shape of the answer looked right, and each time it fell over the moment something actually
consumed it.

> **A classification is not a measurement until something has acted on it.** The cheapest possible
> check — sample five rows from each bucket and confirm they belong there — would have caught all
> three, and takes about a minute. I did it only after being wrong twice.

Also worth saying: r611's writeup opened by correcting r610 and closed by asserting a number that was
itself wrong. **Correcting an error is not evidence the correction is right.**

`unopened-branches.tsv` now holds the verified classification; both earlier files are deleted.

## r620 — made the gate lane-aware: a row whose premise does not hold is not a result

**Round outcome: `tool-fix`.** merged=0. open=3. Nothing actionable on any PR — #6178 10/10 awaiting
the pipeline, #6093 cache-gated, #5950 human-gated ~41h.

### The problem r616 found and this round fixed
Five of the thirteen checks presuppose a **rooting** PR: `parallelns`, `nsslice`, `decldiff`,
`rootsurplus`, `slice`. Each asks a question of the form *"given that this PR roots declarations,
…"*. Run on another lane they emit rows that are **category errors, not defects** — r616 gated the
five recovered branches and `riemann-roch-mul-pow-membership` came back 12 ok / 1 because `decldiff`
objected to a **newly named lemma**, which is precisely what that branch exists to add.

With the rooting lane nearly exhausted (r603), most future work is other lanes, so the gate would
have misreported **by default**.

### The fix
A conservative detector — is this a rooting PR? — and an `n/a` verdict that records **nothing**:

```
_RA = added `_root_.`-anchored declarations      _NR = removed `namespace` lines
IS_ROOTING = (_RA > 0 || _NR > 0)
```

`n/a` neither passes nor fails, so the summary counts only answers the gate actually has a basis for.

| branch | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `subring` (rooting) | 12 ok / 1 failed | **12 ok / 1 failed — unchanged, no `n/a` rows** |
| `riemann-roch-mul-pow-membership` (naming) | 12 ok / 1 `decldiff` | **8 ok / 0 failed**, 5 × `n/a` + a banner |

So **all five recovered branches are gate-clean** once judged in their own lane; the one "answerable"
row was never a finding at all.

> **`ok` and `FAIL` both assert the check had standing to judge.** A third verdict was missing, and
> its absence made a naming branch look defective. The tell was there in r616 — I wrote "these rows
> are category errors, not defects" and then reported the count anyway.

### What is NOT covered, said plainly
`controls.sh` has **no control for `prepush.sh` orchestration** — it tests the individual tools, and
always has. This change is verified by two real runs (a rooting PR unchanged; a non-rooting PR
correctly `n/a`) and not by the suite. A synthetic control would need a throwaway repo carrying
`scripts/lint-dot-notation.py`, which is why it has never existed. **Recording the gap rather than
implying coverage.** Suite still **112 passed, 0 failed**.

## r621 — #6178 merged; #6188 opened and CI caught a defect the bench had carried for 29 rounds

**Round outcome: `merged + shipped + defect found`.** merged=**1** (#6178 at 00:57:26Z).
open 2 → prospected → **3**. #6188 (`LinearEquiv`) ready, CI green 02:02:55Z.

### 🔴 The bench has no CI, and "gate-clean" hid a red build for 29 rounds
`improve/linearequiv-root` was extracted in **r592** and re-gated in r603, r608, r614, r618 and r620 —
**six clean gate runs**. Opened as #6188 in this round, it failed CI immediately:

```
Lattice.lean:300: Unknown identifier `LieSubalgebra.rationalizationEquiv`
Lattice.lean:155: Type mismatch  (AlgHom.restrictScalars_apply)
```

`settle`/`xqualify` had rewritten two reference families into the **wrong namespace** when the branch
was first extracted:

| main | what the branch carried | count |
|---|---|---|
| `Submodule.rationalizationEquiv` | `LieSubalgebra.rationalizationEquiv` | 3 |
| `LinearEquiv.restrictScalars_apply` | `AlgHom.restrictScalars_apply` | 2 |

Both are the **r556 defect class** — a fixer choosing a candidate by matching the *tail* of a name.
`LieSubalgebra.` occurs legitimately 200+ times tree-wide, and `main`'s `Lattice.lean` contains **zero**;
all three in the branch were mine and all three were wrong.

> **`deadpath` passed on both.** It asks whether a qualified name *exists somewhere*, and
> `LieSubalgebra.rationalizationEquiv`-shaped names do exist in the tree's index — it cannot ask
> whether the name is **reachable from this file's imports** or whether it is the **right** declaration.
> Existence is not resolution.

### The staging discipline had a hole I had been praising
Every round I have said the bench pays for itself, and it does — #6148 and #6178 were opened minutes
after a slot freed. But **a staged branch never runs CI**, and I had been treating "12 ok / 1 answered"
as ready-to-open. It means *the static checks are satisfied*, not *it builds*. Twenty-nine rounds of
re-gating re-confirmed the same static facts and could never have found this.

> **The gate is a filter, not a proof.** The only thing that has ever caught a wrong-namespace
> qualification in this session is a red build — r609's r389 mistake and this one, both.

Fixed all five references, re-gated **13 ok / 0 failed** (`slice` cleared too, since the base moved),
CI green, marked ready. `lint-dot-notation` **761 → 753**.

other namespaces (`Submodule` 5 across 2 files, `Submodule.IsLattice` 3, `Basis` 1, `TensorProduct` 1),
and that the `LinearEquiv` cut is **complete** — all 8 of its flagged declarations move.

## r622 — built the check that would have caught #6188 twenty-nine rounds early

**Round outcome: `tool-fix`.** merged=0. open=3. #6188 first review eligible ~03:03Z. Gate now
**14 checks**; controls **112 → 115**.

### First: audited the branch I warned about
`improve/localgeneratorsdata-root` was extracted the same way as #6188 and has never been built. Its
diff makes **10 same-tail namespace rewrites**, and every one is a legitimate rooting move — either an
extension (`LocalGeneratorsData.x` → `SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.x`, the r600 fix) or a
truncation (`TauCeti.A.x` → `A.x`, the rooting itself). **No jump to an unrelated family.**

### That audit *is* the check
The defect and the legitimate rewrites are distinguishable without a build:

```
TauCeti.Submodule.foo -> Submodule.foo                  truncation  OK
LocalGeneratorsData.x -> SheafOfModules.…GeneratorsData.x  extension  OK
Submodule.rationalizationEquiv -> LieSubalgebra.rationalizationEquiv   JUMP  <- the bug
```

`nsjump.py` pairs every qualified name the diff removes with one it adds on the same **tail**, and
reports the pair when neither prefix contains the other.

| commit | CI | nsjump |
|---|---|---|
| `1867bafb0c` (before the fix) | **red** | **3 jumps** — exactly the two families that failed |
| `1f7990e186` (after the fix) | green | **0** |
| `localgeneratorsdata` | never built | **0** |

### The first cut had two false-positive families, and both dissolved with one rule
Naive pairing flagged a green branch twice. Causes: a **rearrangement** (the diff removes and re-adds
both `MulEquiv.trans_apply` and `LinearEquiv.trans_apply`, so each pairs with the other), and **two
distinct declarations sharing a tail** (`…IsInvertible.ofIso` vs `…LocalGeneratorsData.ofIso`).

Fix: an added name is suspicious only if **no** same-tail counterpart is related to it. An identical
prefix is related to itself, which kills the rearrangement case; the genuine rooting counterpart is an
extension or truncation, which kills the cross-pairing case. Both false-positive families went to zero
while the three true positives survived.

> **A check that fires on a green branch teaches nothing.** The refinement was not tuning a threshold
> — it was noticing that the question was wrong: not *"does this pair look odd?"* but *"is there any
> pairing that explains this rewrite?"*

Not gated on `IS_ROOTING`: any lane that rewrites references can suffer this.

> `deadpath` asks whether a qualified name exists **somewhere in the index**. `nsjump` asks whether
> this PR **changed which family it points at**. #6188 shows those are different questions, and only
> the second one was being asked by a build.

## r623 — pointed the new check at merged code; it found three defects, all in itself

**Round outcome: `tool-fix`.** merged=0. open=3. #6188 first review eligible ~03:03Z.
Controls **115 → 116**.

### The audit that mattered: is anything already merged broken?
Ran `nsjump` retrospectively over all seven `improve/*` PRs merged this session (#6022, #6056, #6065,
#6082, #6113, #6148, #6178). **Result: no namespace jump survives in merged code.** That is the
reassurance the check was built to provide, and it is worth more than the check's forward use.

### But it reported three, and all three were the check's fault
`#6082` and `#6065` — **merged, CI-green** — came back with:

```
S.comp                → ContinuousLinearMap.isInvertible_equiv.comp
T.comp                → ContinuousLinearMap.isInvertible_equiv.comp
W.polynomial.eval     → WeierstrassCurve.Affine.CoordinateRing.eval
```

`S`, `T` and `W` are **local binders**. Lean writes dot notation on variables constantly, and r622's
pattern `[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_']*` treats a one-letter binder as a namespace head. Requiring **2+
characters** kills all three; every namespace in this tree is a CamelCase word, and no declaration
lives in `S`. The three true positives on #6188's red head survive untouched.

> **A green branch firing is the check's problem, not the branch's** — r622 said so and I still had to
> learn it twice, because the first time the evidence was two rows on one branch and this time it was
> three rows on *merged* code. **Point a new check at history before trusting it on new work.**

### Two self-inflicted errors, both caught in under a minute
1. **I broke the docstring exactly as in r593** — anchored the insertion on `import sys` instead of the
   closing `"""`, so prose became bare code. `controls.sh` went red on the next run with the *first*
   assertion failing, which is what a suite is for. Fixed by moving the prose inside the quotes.
2. **I read a `0` as a regression.** `nsjump` diffs `<base>` against the **working tree**, so naming a
   past commit on the command line measures whatever branch is checked out. The true positives were
   never lost; I was pointing at the wrong tree. Now documented at the top of the file.

> Both errors are the same shape as the ones this session keeps producing: **I used a command without
> checking what it operates on.** The difference is that the feedback loop is now seconds — a control
> suite and a firing control — rather than a round.

**Round outcome: `fixed + contested`.** merged=0. open=3. #6188 head `cba6f67876`, **CI green
03:06:58Z**, board now BEHIND — re-drive eligible ~04:07Z.

### Did not drive: another worker was already on it
`ps` showed a live review at 6m41s when I swept, so I waited rather than raced. It ran ~17 minutes —
long, but the log kept moving, and the r599 rule is that **mtime, not elapsed time, distinguishes slow
from hung.** Board: 8 green, `api-design` + `generality` blocking.

### `api-design` — implemented, one declaration
`LinearEquiv.toLinearEquiv_generalLinearEquiv_symm` was `private`; the finding asked to export it and
mark it `@[simp]`. It states `((generalLinearEquiv R M).symm f).toLinearEquiv = f`, a structural fact
about Mathlib's general-linear equivalence rather than a `congrAut` implementation detail. Exported,
tagged, **CI green — `simpNF` accepted it**. Note it *is* linter-flagged, so unlike #6148's six this
was never surplus: the lint asked for the rooting, `api-design` asked for the visibility.

### `generality` — contested, and the distinction from #6093 is the whole point
It asked for `extendOfIsLattice` over a domain and its fraction field instead of `ℤ ⊂ ℚ`, and for
`congrAut` over semilinear equivalences. **This PR does not alter a single hypothesis of either.**

```
-noncomputable def extendOfIsLattice {S : Submodule ℤ V} {T : Submodule ℤ W}
+noncomputable def _root_.LinearEquiv.extendOfIsLattice {S : Submodule ℤ V} {T : Submodule ℤ W}
```

I accepted a finding of this *shape* on #6093, so the contest had to say why this one differs rather
than re-run a losing argument:

> #6093's `generality` turned on the **receiver**: relocating into `ContinuousMap` entrenched a
> receiver stronger than the construction needed, and the PR was choosing it. Here the receiver is not
> in question — `LinearEquiv` is correct, which is precisely why the linter flags these. The finding
> is about the **hypothesis set**, and that is the one thing the diff does not touch.

Conceded both on the merits, sized them (a restatement of four declarations plus their proofs; a
result-type change plus both evaluation lemmas), and pointed at the #6093 precedent for handling a
signature change as its own PR. Also said plainly that I had just implemented the sibling finding, so
the contest is not a reflex to decline work.

> **A precedent you accepted is the strongest thing an opponent can quote at you.** The useful move is
> not to distinguish it cheaply but to name exactly which of its premises fails here — and if none
> does, to concede. The receiver/hypothesis distinction is real, and stating it that way makes the
> contest falsifiable.

## r625 — closed the second of the session's two red builds; the check needed three corrections first

**Round outcome: `tool-fix`.** merged=0. open=3. #6188 board BEHIND, re-drive eligible ~04:07Z.
Gate now **15 checks**; controls **116 → 119**.

### The gap
Two builds went red this session. r621's is now caught by `nsjump`. r609's was the other: #6148 kept
`namespace IsCompactOperator` for six unflagged private helpers, rooted the flagged ones out to
`_root_.IsCompactOperator.x`, and a bare `x` inside the surviving wrapper stopped resolving.

**Nothing could see it.** `siblingscan` and `xsibling` both model a wrapper being **removed**; here it
survives, which is the whole shape. `deadpath` only inspects qualified names, and the broken reference
is bare. The detector was a 13-minute build.

`rootedin.py` asks the dual question: inside a namespace that is still present, is there a bare
reference to a declaration this PR rooted *out* of it? On r609's red commit it reports **9** — the one
CI named plus eight more of the same class waiting behind it.

### Three false-positive families, each found by pointing it at real branches
Following r623's rule — aim a new check at history before trusting it — I ran it on the red commit,
two green heads and the unbuilt bench branch. It fired **5 times on the bench branch**, and every one
was the check's fault:

1. **`--` line comments unmasked.** `-- \`ofIso\` leaves the index type untouched` read as a reference.
   (Block comments were masked; line comments were not.)
2. **Declaration headers counted as references.** `class IsInvertible` and
   `theorem IsInvertible.of_iso` *declare* a name; they do not refer to the rooted one.
3. **A same-named declaration in the enclosing stack shadows the rooted one.** The file declares
   `TauCeti.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible` *and* roots `SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.IsInvertible`;
   a bare `IsInvertible` resolves to the first and is fine. **This is r563 exactly** — assuming a short
   name must mean the declaration this PR moved.

Fixing (2) by skipping declaration lines then broke the positive control, because a reference often
sits **on the header itself** (`theorem uses : True := moved`). The correct form is r563's: **mask the
declared name, do not skip the line.**

Final discrimination: **RED 9 / green 0 / green 0 / bench 0.**

> Four passes to get one check right, and three of the four errors were ones this session has already
> recorded — masking comments (r552), masking the declared name (r563), and a short name that means
> something else (r563 again). **Writing a new checker is mostly re-encountering the old traps**, which
> is an argument for reading the ledger's tool lessons before writing one, not after.

## r626 — a fourth false positive, a fourth trap already in the ledger

**Round outcome: `tool-fix`.** merged=0. open=3. #6188 re-drive eligible ~04:07Z.
Controls **119 → 121**.

### Ran the new check against history, as r623 requires
`rootedin` over all seven merged `improve/*` PRs plus the r609 red commit and the bench branch.
**#6056 — merged, CI-green — reported one hit:**

```
Group.lean:213  bare `ext` cannot reach `RootPairing.weylGroup.ext`
```

Line 213 is **`@[ext]`**. An attribute, sitting above `theorem _root_.RootPairing.weylGroup.ext`.

**This is r550 verbatim**: that round shipped a tool which rewrote `@[ext]` into
`@[RootPairing.weylGroup.ext]` for exactly this reason, and the fix was exactly this — mask attribute
brackets before looking for references. Masked; re-audited: **all 7 merged PRs 0, the red commit still
9, the bench 0.**

### Four false-positive families in one check, all four previously recorded
| # | what fired | the ledger entry it repeats |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `--` line comments read as code | r552 (comment masking) |
| 2 | declaration headers read as references | r563 (mask the declared name) |
| 3 | a same-named declaration shadowing the rooted one | r563 (a short name means something else) |
| 4 | `@[ext]` read as a reference | **r550 (attribute brackets)** |

Every one of them is a lesson this project already paid for, in a checker written by someone who had
paid for them.

> **The traps are properties of the domain, not of the tool.** Anything that scans Lean text for a
> bare identifier will meet comments, attributes, declaration headers and name collisions — in that
> order, apparently. The ledger has a *list* of them, and I rediscovered it four times in two rounds
> instead of reading it first. **Next new scanner: start from r550/r552/r563, not from a blank file.**

### And the audit is the reason it is now right
Three of the four surfaced only because the check was pointed at **merged, green** code, where any row
is by construction a false positive. That is a stronger oracle than a fixture — the fixture asserts
what I thought of; merged history asserts what actually occurs.

## r627 — audited the sibling scanners for r626's trap and found nothing; recording the negative

**Round outcome: `verified`.** merged=0. open=3. #6188 re-drive eligible ~04:07Z. No tool changed.

### The question
r626 found `rootedin` reading `@[ext]` as a reference — r550's trap. The obvious follow-up: do the
other text scanners share it? Grepping for attribute/comment masking showed they differ widely
(`deadpath` and `nsjump` mask no attributes; `rootedin` and `xsibling` mask everything).

### The answer is that the difference is correct, not a gap
- **`deadpath`** looks for *qualified* names and asks whether each resolves. An attribute
  **is** a name reference — `@[Foo.bar]` naming a declaration that does not exist is a genuine defect,
  not noise. Masking attributes there would *lose* coverage.
- **`nsjump`** needs a **pair** — a removed qualified name and an added one sharing a tail. Tested the
  r550 shape directly (`@[ext]` → `@[RootPairing.weylGroup.ext]`): **0 rows**, because the removed side
  contributes no qualified name at all. Safe by construction.
- **`rootedin`** looks for a *bare* identifier, which is exactly where an attribute is
  indistinguishable from a use. It is the one that needed masking, and it has it.

> **The trap is not "scanners must mask attributes"; it is "a bare-identifier scanner must".** Which
> masking a tool needs follows from the question it asks, and r626's lesson was in danger of becoming
> a cargo-culted rule applied to tools that would be made worse by it.

### Nothing changed, and that is the result
Tempting to find something to fix after two rounds of fixing. The honest outcome is that the audit
was cheap, the answer was negative, and forcing a change to `deadpath` or `nsjump` would have removed
real coverage in the name of consistency. **A negative audit is worth recording precisely because the
next round would otherwise re-ask it.**
